CUSTOMER / HIRER DETAILS
Name of Hirer{{ doc.applicant_name or "" }}
Residential Address {{ doc.address_line_1 or "" }}{% if doc.address_line_2 %}, {{ doc.address_line_2 }}{% endif %}{% if doc.custom_suburb %}, {{ doc.custom_suburb }}{% endif %}{% if doc.city %}, {{ doc.city }}{% endif %}{% if doc.custom_province and doc.custom_province != doc.city %}, {{ doc.custom_province }}{% endif %}{% if doc.country %}, {{ doc.country }}{% endif %}
(hereinafter known as the “Hirer”)
HP Account No {{ doc.hp_account_no or "" }}
HP Reference / Quotation No {{ doc.hp_reference_no or "" }}
TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF HIRE:
1 CONTRACT SUM:
The Hirer shall pay the total sum of $ {{ doc.total_payable_amount }} as per the Credit Contract, which sum is inclusive of principal, interest, and other charges for the term of the Hire.
2 DESCRIPTION OF GOODS:

{{ item.product_description or "" }} X {{ item.quantity or "-" }}

3 PAYMENTS:
Upon the execution of this agreement by the Hirer in consideration of the option to purchase, the Hirer shall pay to the owner and/or its nominee the sum of:
I. Cost of Goods $ {{ doc.custom_flexi_cash_price or "0.00" }}
II. Deposit $ {{ doc.custom_flexi_deposit_amount or "0.00" }}
III. Balance after deposit $ {{ doc.custom_flexi_value_after_deposit or "0.00" }}
IV. Documentation Fees $ {{ doc.custom_flexi_documentation_fee or "0.00" }}
V. Admin Fees $ {{ doc.custom_flexi_admin_fee or "0.00" }}
VI. Interest Charges $ {{ doc.total_payable_interest or "0.00" }}
VII. Total Payable $ {{ doc.total_payable_amount or "0.00" }}
VIII. Monthly Installment $ {{ doc.custom_flexi_monthly_instalment_amount or "0.00" }}
IX. First Installment Date {{ frappe.utils.formatdate(doc.custom_flexi_first_instalment_date, "dd-mm-yyyy") if doc.custom_flexi_first_instalment_date else "" }}
4 In the event the Hirer defaults in any one payment, then the Hirer shall be liable to pay a default interest rate of 2.2% on the unpaid amount. Such interest shall accrue from the date of the default till the total amount in default is cleared in full.
5 The Chattels, being the subject of this agreement, shall remain the property of the Owner till such time when all the payments specified in clauses 3 and 4 have been duly paid (provided always that the terms and conditions of this agreement have in the meantime been duly observed by the hirer). The Hirer shall be a mere Bailee of the chattels till such time as the chattels are fully paid for.
6 The Hirer shall keep the Chattels in good order and in working condition at the Hirer’s address (any change of which shall be promptly notified to the Owner in writing) and which may be inspected by the Owner and or its agent at all reasonable times.
7 The Hirer shall not sell, assign, transfer, pledge, mortgage, or otherwise deal with or part with the possession of the said chattels or any of the benefits of this agreement nor commit or suffer the chattels to be seized under distress for rent, rates taxes or any other legal process.
8 If the said chattels shall during the hiring become damaged, defective or unserviceable, the hirer shall report such fact to the Owner who may at the expense of the Hirer repair, make good or cause to be repaired the said chattels and the Hirer on demand by the Owner shall deliver the said chattels to the Owner for such purpose.
9 The Hirer shall have a right to terminate this agreement at any time by returning the chattels in good and working condition at his or her own expense to the Owner. The Hirer will be liable to pay to the Owner the shortfall balance or any balance owing after the market value consideration has been deducted from the balance owed at the time the chattels are returned.
10 If the Hirer commits breach of any term of this Agreement or fails to pay any two consecutive monthly instalments, and or defaults in the final payment the Owner will have the right to terminate this agreement and take possession of the chattels the subject of the hire by giving 21 DAYS prior notice to repossession and unless in the meanwhile the breach is remedied and the hire charges (default amount) are paid as the case may be, this agreement shall, on the expiration of the notice period stand terminated. If the agreement is terminated as aforesaid, the Hirer’s option to purchase as hereinbefore mentioned shall stand forfeited or cancelled.
11 In the event the agreement is terminated due to the reason of default and non-payment of the hire charges by the Hirer, the Hirer shall continue to be liable to the Owner for all hire charges, default interest, fees, charges, and enforcement expenses due under the agreement.
12 The Hirer understands and agrees that the Owners, being the not Manufacturers of the chattels, do not supply the chattels or any of them subject to any condition or warranty either express or implied as to the quality, description fitness, suitability for use or otherwise.
13 The Hirer agrees that the risk in the chattels passes to the Hirer at the time of delivery and or possession of the chattels, and the Hirer must insure the chattels to cover all risks to the full replacement value of the chattels.
14 In the event of any loss or damage to the chattels by any means whatsoever, the Hirer remains liable to the Owner for the monthly payments and the contract sum.
15 No relaxation, delay or indulgence on the part of the Owner in enforcing any terms and conditions of this agreement shall prejudice or be deemed to be the waiver of any rights of the Owner under this agreement and or operate as a waiver of any breach of agreement.
16 This agreement shall only become binding upon acceptance and signing by the Owner and or its authorized representatives.
17 The Owner reserves the right to terminate this agreement and take possession of any chattels under this agreement if any information originally tendered in the application by the Hirer is later confirmed by the Owner to be false.
18 The Hirer shall pay to the owner on demand
a) All cost of locating the hirer or the Goods if the account is in default.
b) All cost or recovering possession of Goods or any amount payable under this contract including any bailiff fee etc.
c) All Value added tax, Stamp duty, or other taxes or duties payable by the owner in respect of this agreement on the supply of Goods and Services.
d) All cost, duties and taxes referred to in clause 18 (a), 18 (b) and 18 (c) or other fees, charges, duties that may be introduced, and interest on arrears may be debited to hirer’s account when they accrue. The Hirer can also be charged for the insurance of arrears letters, reminder letters or demand letters or other associated cost where account can be passed to external parties for debt of outstanding amount.
19 The owner shall be liberty to transfer any credit balance from any of the hirer’s paid off contract to the hirer’s existing account which may be having due or arrears with or without consent of the hirer provided that such credit balance is not transferred to third party’s account in which any case the owner shall ask for written confirmation from the hirer.
20 The Hirer may take insurance cover to insure the chattels and shall provide the certificate of covering stating the terms and conditions thereof.
IMPORTANT NOTICE: THINGS YOU MUST KNOW BEFORE YOU SIGN
READ THIS HIRE PURCHASE AGREEMENT so that you know exactly what you are entering into and what you will have to do under the agreement.
Once you sign the agreement, you will be bound by it. However, you may end the agreement before you obtain (or try to obtain) any credit by informing COMFORT HOME FURNISHING PTE LIMITED TRADING AS FLEXIBLE PURCHASE in writing, but you will still be liable for any fees or charges incurred.
You acknowledge that you have been advised by COMFORT HOME FURNISHING PTE LIMITED TRADING AS FLEXIBLE PURCHASE that you may consult with an insurance on the option of taking out an insurance cover for the product.
If you take out insurance, the credit provider cannot insist on any particular insurance company.
Fill in or cross out any blank spaces. Get a copy of this agreement document.
DO NOT SIGN this agreement document if there is anything you do not understand.

FORM 1
INFORMATION STATEMENT
THINGS YOU SHOULD KNOW ABOUT YOUR PROPOSED CREDIT CONTRACT
THE CONTRACT
1 How can I get details of my proposed credit contract?
Your credit provider must give you a pre-contractual statement containing certain information about your contract. The pre-contractual statement and this document must be given to you before-
· Your contract is entered into; or
· You make an offer to enter into the contract;
Which ever happens first.
2 How can I get a copy of the final contract?
If the contract document is to be signed by you and returned to your credit provider, you must be given a copy to keep.
Also, the credit provider must give you a copy of the final contract within 14 days it is made. This rule does not, however, apply, if the contract can be accepted by you –
· Accessing or drawing down credit to incur a liability, or
· Satisfying other conditions
The rule will also not apply if, when the credit provider gives you a copy of document to sign and return to the credit provider, you are given a copy of the contract document signed by the credit provider to keep.
If you want another copy of your contract write to your credit provider and ask for one. Your credit provider may charge you a fee. Your credit provider has to give you a copy-
· Within 14 days of your written request if the original contract came into existence 1 year or less before your request; or
· Otherwise within 30 days of your written request.
3 Can I terminate the contract?
Yes. So long as you have not obtained or tried to obtain any credit under the contract, you can terminate the contract by writing to the credit provider. However, you will still have to pay any fees or charges incurred before you terminated the contract.
4 How can I find out the payout for the contract?
You can pay your credit provider the amount required to pay out your credit contract on the day you wish to end your contract.
5 How can I find out the payout figure?
You can write to your credit provider the amount required to pay out your credit contract on the day you wish to end your contract.
Your credit provider must give you a statement within 7 days after your request to the credit provider. You may be charged a fee for the statement.
6 Will I pay less interest if I pay out my account early?
Yes. The interest you can be charged depends on the actual time money is owed. However, you may have to pay an early termination charge (if your contract permits your credit provider to charge one) and other fees.
7 Can my contract be changed by my credit provider?
Yes. But only if your contract says so.
8 Will I be told in advance if my credit provider is going to make a change in the contract?
That depends on the type of change. For example-
· You get at least same day notice for a change to an annual percentage rate. The notice may be written notice to you or a notice published in a newspaper.
· You get 30 days advance written notice for-
I. A change in the way in which interest is calculated; or
II. A change in credit fees; or
III. Any other changes by your credit provider
Except where the change reduces what you have to pay, or the change happens automatically under the contract.
9 Is there anything I can do if I think that my contract is unjust?
Yes. You should first talk to your credit provider. Discuss the matter and see if you can come to some arrangement. If that is not successful, you could apply to the court. Contact the Department of Fair Trading and Consumer Affairs or get legal advice on how to go about this.
INSURANCE
10 Do I have to take out insurance?
Your credit provider can insist that you take out or pay the cost of types of insurance specifically allowed by law. These include compulsory third-party personal injury insurance, mortgage indemnity insurance, or insurance covering property secured by any mortgage. Otherwise, you can decide if you want to take out insurance or not.
11 Will I get details of my insurance now?
Yes. If you have taken out insurance over mortgaged property or consumer credit insurance, and the premium is financed by your credit provider, the insurer must give you a copy of the policy within 14 days after the insurer has accepted the insurance proposal.
Also, if you acquire an interest in any such insurance policy which is taken out by your credit provider, then within 14 days after the insurer has accepted the insurance proposal.
You can always ask the insurer for details of your insurance contract. If you ask in writing, your insurer must give you a statement containing all the provisions of the contract.
12 If the insurer does not accept my proposal, will I be told?
Yes, if the insurance were to be financed by the credit contract. The insurer will inform you if the proposal is rejected.
13 In that case, what happens to the premiums?
Your credit provider must give you a refund or credit unless the insurance is to be arranged with another insurer.
14 What happens if my credit contract ends before any insurance contract over the mortgaged property?
You can end the insurance contract and get a proportionate rebate of any premium from the insurer.
MORTGAGES
15 If my contract says I have to give a mortgage, what does this mean?
A mortgage means that you give your credit provider certain rights over any property you mortgage. If you default under your contract, you can lose that property and you might still owe money to the credit provider.
16 Should I get a copy of mortgage?
Yes. It can be part of your credit contract or, if it is a separate document, you will be given a copy of the mortgage within 14 days after your mortgage is entered into.
However, you need not be given a copy if, when the credit provider gives you a copy of the mortgage document to sign and return to the credit provider, you are also given a copy of the mortgage document to keep.
17 Is there anything that I am not allowed to do with the property mortgaged?
The law says you cannot assign or dispose of the property unless you have your credit provider's or the court's permission. You must also look after the property. Read the mortgage document as well. It will usually have other terms and conditions about what you can or cannot do with the property.
18 What can I do if I find that I cannot afford my repayments and there is a mortgage over the property?
See the answers to questions 22 and 23
Otherwise you may –
· If the mortgaged property is goods, give the property back to your credit provider, together with a letter saying you want the credit provider to sell the property for you;
· Sell the property, but only if your credit provider gives permission first;
OR
· Give the property to someone who may then take over the repayments, but only if your credit provider gives permission first.
If your provider won't give permission contact the Department of Fair Trading and Consumer Affairs for help.
If you have a guarantor, talk to the guarantor who may be able to help you.
You should understand that you may owe money to your credit provider even after the mortgaged property is sold.
19 Can my credit provider take or sell the mortgaged property?
Yes, if you have not carried out all of your obligations under the contract.
20 If my credit provider writes asking me where the mortgaged goods are, do I have to say where they are?
Yes. You have 7 days after receiving your credit provider's request to tell your credit provider. If you do not have the goods you must give credit provider all the information you have so they can be traced.
21 When can my credit provider or its agent come into a residence to take possession of mortgaged goods?
Your credit provider can only do so if it has the court's approval or the written consent of the occupier which is given after the occupier is informed in writing of the relevant section in the Consumer Credit Act.
GENERAL
22 What do I do if I cannot make a repayment?
Get in touch with your credit provider immediately. Discuss the matter and see if you can come to some arrangement. You can ask your credit provider to change your contract in several ways, for example-
· To extend the term of the contract and either reduce the amount of each payment accordingly, or defer payments for a specified period, or
· To simply defer payments for a specified period.
23 What if my credit provider and I cannot agree on a suitable arrangement?
If you have been unemployed, sick or there is another good reason why you are having problems with your contract, then your contract may be able to be changed to meet your situation.
You may be able to apply to the court. Contact the Department of Fair Trading and Consumer Affairs or get legal advice on how to go about this.
There are other people, such as financial advisors, who may be able to help.
24 Can my credit provider take action against me?
Yes, if you are in default under your contract. But the law says that you cannot be unduly harassed or threatened for repayments. If you are being unduly harassed or threatened, contact the Department of Fair Trading and Consumer Affairs, or get legal advice.
25 Do I have any other legal rights and obligations?
Yes. The law will give you other rights and obligations. You should READ YOUR CONTRACT carefully.
IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS OR WANT MORE INFORMATION, CONTACT THE DEPARTMENT OF FAIR TRADING AND CONSUMER AFFAIRS OR GET LEGAL ADVICE. PLEASE KEEP THIS INFORMATION STATEMENT. YOU MAY WANT SOME INFORMATION FROM IT AT A LATER DATE.
